Knowledge index: part C contains 28 original fact blocks across 1 chunks; part C2 contains 27 continuation fact blocks across 1 chunks, all from this section’s mapped physical pages.
Authority and exam facts are located in A.01; audience in B.01; accuracy limits in D.01; demand and competitor gaps in E.01 and E2.01.
VERIFY list:
Accepted inventory: 28 C facts; 27 C2 facts; 16 typed debts; ids DE-EMERGENCY-COUNT, DE-EMERGENCY-PASS, DE-EMERGENCY-TIME, DE-EMERGENCY-CADENCE, DE-EMERGENCY-COVER, DE-EMERGENCY-EQUIPMENT, DE-EMERGENCY-ROAD-EDGE, DE-EMERGENCY-FIRE, DE-EMERGENCY-RAIL, DE-EMERGENCY-SKID, DE-EMERGENCY-IMPACT, DE-EMERGENCY-FIRST-AID, DE-EMERGENCY-REPORT-SCOPE, DE-EMERGENCY-CONTACTS, DE-EMERGENCY-MARKET, DE-EMERGENCY-TEARDOWN.
- DE-EMERGENCY-COUNT: The handbook does not state the knowledge-test question count; obtain an applicable official issuer statement before displaying a count.
- DE-EMERGENCY-PASS: The handbook does not state a knowledge-test passing percentage or passing score; obtain an applicable official issuer statement before displaying a threshold.
- DE-EMERGENCY-TIME: The handbook does not state a knowledge-test time limit; do not substitute the road-exam duration.
- DE-EMERGENCY-CADENCE: The snapshot is dated July on the front cover; the frequency of handbook revision was not independently verified.
- DE-EMERGENCY-COVER: The extracted cover text carries the edition but not the graphical title or issuer; the issuer is established separately by frontmatter and the official linking page.
- DE-EMERGENCY-EQUIPMENT: Parking-brake handle, wet-brake, ignition-lock and failed-brake instructions depend on vehicle equipment. Do not merge failed-brake pumping with normal ABS emergency braking or apply every mechanical step to every vehicle without manufacturer-specific verification.
- DE-EMERGENCY-ROAD-EDGE: The shoulder-return passage tells the driver to turn sharply after listed preconditions without describing edge drop, surface or vehicle constraints. That steering instruction is withheld pending technical safety review.
- DE-EMERGENCY-FIRE: The fire and crash passages describe self-extinguishing methods, a fixed separation distance and use of flares despite possible spilled fuel. These operational details are withheld pending current fire-safety guidance and site/equipment conditions.
- DE-EMERGENCY-RAIL: The stalled-track text suggests a restart attempt when no train is seen, but does not specify a full evacuation, emergency-notification or safe-restart procedure. The restart instruction is withheld pending applicable official rail-safety verification.
- DE-EMERGENCY-SKID: The generic skid-recovery passage does not distinguish skid type or ABS equipment and gives a blanket brake prohibition and repeated steering corrections. Those detailed recovery instructions are withheld pending technical review.
- DE-EMERGENCY-IMPACT: The impact-protection passage states that an airbag will inflate and gives collision-steering/bracing advice without deployment or crash-condition limits. These guarantees and specific impact maneuvers are withheld pending equipment and safety review.
- DE-EMERGENCY-FIRST-AID: The first-aid passage says not to move injured people except for specified immediate dangers, while a later aid duty includes transporting them for care. Medical handling, bleeding and shock directions are withheld pending qualified clinical/legal reconciliation.
- DE-EMERGENCY-REPORT-SCOPE: The own-property-only paragraph says immediately report without identifying its reporting channel or relation to the later threshold-based police-report list. That isolated obligation is withheld until its scope is clarified.
- DE-EMERGENCY-CONTACTS: Telephone numbers, service hours, email and web reporting availability are dynamic and have not been freshly verified. Agency identity and issue categories are supported; live contact details are not minted as stable facts.
- DE-EMERGENCY-MARKET: market pack requires sourced recon.
- DE-EMERGENCY-TEARDOWN: competitive teardown requires sourced inspection.
Dynamic isolation: Contact details and mutable service/provider information remain outside stable facts; monetary and numerical rules are stated only as source-edition facts.
